First, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $x$, treating $y$ as a constant. 

Making a substitution $x+y=u,$ $\text{d}x=\text{d}u,$ we get.

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{1}{(x+y)^{2}}\,\text{d}x\text{d}y & ={\int }_{1}^{2}[{\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{1}{(x+y)^{2}}\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}[{\int }_{y}^{1+y}\frac{1}{{u}^{2}}\,\text{d}u]\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}{[-\frac{1}{u}]}_{y}^{1+y}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}(-\frac{1}{y+1}+\frac{1}{y})\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}[\frac{1}{y}-\frac{1}{y+1}]\,\text{d}y\end{aligned}
$$

 

Then, we integrate with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{2}[\frac{1}{y}-\frac{1}{y+1}]\,\text{d}y & =[\operatorname{ln}⁡y-\operatorname{ln}⁡(y+1)]_{1}^{2} \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{y}{y+1}){|}_{1}^{2} \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{2}{3})-\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{1}{2}) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{2}{3})+\operatorname{ln}⁡(2) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{2}{3}\cdot 2) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{4}{3})\end{aligned}
$$

First, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $x$, treating $y$ as a constant: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{2}[{\int }_{0}^{1}({2}^{y+1}{x}^{2})\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y & ={\int }_{1}^{2}{2}^{y+1}[{\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}{2}^{y+1}{[\frac{{x}^{3}}{3}]}_{0}^{1}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}{2}^{y+1}(\frac{{1}^{3}}{3}-\frac{{0}^{3}}{3})\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{{2}^{y+1}}{3}\,\text{d}y\end{aligned}
$$

 

Then, we integrate with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{{2}^{y+1}}{3}\,\text{d}y & ={[\frac{{2}^{y+1}}{3\operatorname{ln}⁡2}]}_{1}^{2} \\  & =\frac{{2}^{2+1}}{3\operatorname{ln}⁡2}-\frac{{2}^{1+1}}{3\operatorname{ln}⁡2} \\  & =\frac{8-4}{3\operatorname{ln}⁡2} \\  & =\frac{4}{3\operatorname{ln}⁡2}\end{aligned}
$$

$$

Then, we integrate with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}60{y}^{2}\,\text{d}y & =60{[\frac{{y}^{3}}{3}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =60\cdot \frac{1}{3} \\  & =20\end{aligned}
$$

$$

Then, we integrate with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /12} & (-\operatorname{cos}⁡(2y+\frac{5\pi }{3})+\operatorname{cos}⁡(2y+\pi ))\text{d}y \\  & ={[-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2y+\frac{5\pi }{3})+\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2y+\pi )]}_{0}^{\pi /12} \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\cdot \frac{\pi }{12}+\frac{5\pi }{3})+\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\cdot 0+\frac{5\pi }{3}) \\  & +\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\cdot \frac{\pi }{12}+\pi )-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\cdot 0+\pi ) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{11\pi }{6})+\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{5\pi }{3})+\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{7\pi }{6})-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi )] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\frac{1}{2}-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}-\frac{1}{2}-0] \\  & =-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}\end{aligned}

$$

questions.problem:
Evaluate the double integral ${∬}_{D}9{x}^{2}{y}^{2}\,\text{d}A,$ where 
$D={(x,y)\,:\,-2\le x\le 2,\,-1\le y\le 1}.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we express our double integral as a repeated integral:        

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}9{x}^{2}{y}^{2}\,\text{d}A & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}[{\int }_{-2}^{2}9{x}^{2}{y}^{2}\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $x$, treating $y$ as a constant:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-1}^{1}[{\int }_{-2}^{2}9{x}^{2}{y}^{2}\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}9{y}^{2}[{\int }_{-2}^{2}{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}9{y}^{2}{[\frac{{x}^{3}}{3}]}_{-2}^{2}\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}9{y}^{2}(\frac{{2}^{3}}{3}-\frac{(-2)^{3}}{3})\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}9{y}^{2}\cdot \frac{16}{3}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}48{y}^{2}\,\text{d}y\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we integrate with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-1}^{1}48{y}^{2}\,\text{d}y & =[16{y}^{3}]_{-1}^{1} \\  & =16({1}^{3}-(-1)^{3}) \\  & =16\cdot 2 \\  & =32\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Evaluate the double integral ${∬}_{D}\frac{{y}^{2}}{{x}^{2}+4}\,\text{d}A,$ where 
$D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 2,\,0\le y\le 3}.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we express our double integral as a repeated integral:      

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}\frac{{y}^{2}}{{x}^{2}+4}\,\text{d}A & ={\int }_{0}^{3}[{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\frac{{y}^{2}}{{x}^{2}+4}\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $x$, treating $y$ as a constant:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{3}[{\int }_{0}^{2}\frac{{y}^{2}}{{x}^{2}+4}\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y & ={\int }_{0}^{3}{y}^{2}[{\int }_{0}^{2}\frac{1}{{x}^{2}+4}\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}{y}^{2}{[\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{2})]}_{0}^{2}\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{3}{y}^{2}(\operatorname{arctan}⁡(1)-\operatorname{arctan}⁡0)\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{\pi }{8}{\int }_{0}^{3}{y}^{2}\,\text{d}y\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we integrate with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\pi }{8}{\int }_{0}^{3}{y}^{2}\,\text{d}y & =\frac{\pi }{8}(\frac{{y}^{3}}{3}){|}_{0}^{3} \\  & =\frac{\pi }{24}({3}^{3}-{0}^{3}) \\  & =\frac{9\pi }{8}\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Evaluate the double integral ${∬}_{D}\operatorname{cos}⁡(x+y)\,\text{d}A,$ where 
$D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le \frac{\pi }{4},\,0\le y\le \pi }.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we express our double integral as a repeated integral:   

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}\operatorname{cos}⁡(x+y)\,\text{d}A & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }[{\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}\operatorname{cos}⁡(x+y)\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $x$, treating $y$ as a constant:

Making a substitution $x+y=u,$ $\text{d}x=\text{d}u,$ we get.

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi }[{\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}\operatorname{cos}⁡(x+y)\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }[{\int }_{y}^{y+\pi /4}\operatorname{cos}⁡u\,\text{d}u]\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }[\operatorname{sin}⁡u]_{y}^{y+\pi /4}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }[\operatorname{sin}⁡(y+\frac{\pi }{4})-\operatorname{sin}⁡y]\,\text{d}y\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we integrate with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi }[\operatorname{sin}⁡(y+\frac{\pi }{4})-\operatorname{sin}⁡y]\text{d}y & ={[\operatorname{cos}⁡y-\operatorname{cos}⁡(y+\frac{\pi }{4})]}_{0}^{\pi } \\  & =(\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi )-\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{5\pi }{4}))-(\operatorname{cos}⁡0-\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})) \\  & =(-1+\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2})-(1-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}) \\  & =\sqrt{2}-2\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Evaluate the double integral ${∬}_{D}{e}^{x+y}\,\text{d}A,$ where 
$D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,0\le y\le 2}.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we express our double integral as a repeated integral:   

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}{e}^{x+y}\,\text{d}A & ={\int }_{0}^{2}[{\int }_{0}^{1}{e}^{x+y}\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $x$, treating $y$ as a constant:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{2}[{\int }_{0}^{1}{e}^{x+y}\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{[{e}^{x+y}]}_{0}^{1}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}({e}^{1+y}-{e}^{0+y})\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}({e}^{1+y}-{e}^{y})\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}(e{e}^{y}-{e}^{y})\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{e}^{y}(e-1)\text{d}y\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we integrate with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{2}{e}^{y}(e-1)\text{d}y & =(e-1)[{e}^{y}]_{0}^{2} \\  & =(e-1)({e}^{2}-{e}^{0}) \\  & =(e-1)({e}^{2}-1) \\  & ={e}^{3}-{e}^{2}-e+1\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Evaluate the double integral ${∬}_{D}\frac{{x}^{2}}{{y}^{3}}\,\text{d}A,$ where 
$D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 3,\,-3\le y\le -1}.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we express our double integral as a repeated integral:      

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}\frac{{x}^{2}}{{y}^{3}}\,\text{d}A & ={\int }_{-3}^{-1}[{\int }_{0}^{3}\frac{{x}^{2}}{{y}^{3}}\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $x$, treating $y$ as a constant:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-3}^{-1}[{\int }_{0}^{3}\frac{{x}^{2}}{{y}^{3}}\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y & ={\int }_{-3}^{3}\frac{1}{{y}^{3}}[{\int }_{0}^{3}{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{-3}^{-1}\frac{1}{{y}^{3}}{[\frac{{x}^{3}}{3}]}_{0}^{3}\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{-3}^{-1}\frac{1}{{y}^{3}}(\frac{{3}^{3}}{3}-\frac{{0}^{3}}{3})\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{-3}^{-1}\frac{9}{{y}^{3}}\,\text{d}y\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we integrate with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-3}^{-1}\frac{9}{{y}^{3}}\,\text{d}y & =9{[-\frac{1}{2{y}^{2}}]}_{-3}^{-1} \\  & =9(-\frac{1}{2(-1)^{2}}+\frac{1}{2(-3)^{2}}) \\  & =-4\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.worked_solution:
